Iron supplementation should be confirmed with bloodwork before starting. Over-supplementation can cause harm. Take with food and vitamin C to improve absorption and reduce GI side effects.
Iron helps your body make hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen, and women with heavy periods and people who are pregnant are among those most likely to run low.

Each tablet has 65 mg of iron, which is above the 45 mg a day upper limit set for adults; doctors sometimes prescribe more than that for a limited time to treat iron deficiency, which is why bloodwork and a clinician's plan matter here.
Iron can make some medicines work less well, including levothyroxine (a thyroid medicine) and levodopa (used for Parkinson's disease and restless legs syndrome).
Keep the bottle away from kids: iron products are a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6.
From the clinical guidance in the sources.

Women with heavy periods are at higher risk of low iron, the adult upper limit is 45 mg a day unless a doctor prescribes more short term, and iron is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6.
